title: Repeating and number patterns
summary: Shapes and numbers that follow a rule. Find the pattern, continue it and fix it.
guide: This studio is for Years 2–3 (ages 7–9). The sentences are short; read them aloud if your child needs it. The small picture above each mission shows what to do.
In a repeating {{term:pattern}}, one chunk comes again and again. We call it the unit of repeat. Children should find the unit and use it to continue the pattern.
To place a shape, first tap an empty space, then tap a shape underneath. The chosen space has a thick outline.
In growing and number patterns, each figure or number comes from the one before by a rule, for example “add 4 each time”. Numbers and figures run from left to right.
Ask your child “How did you know?”. Saying the rule in their own words is the heart of spotting patterns.

engine.label-step: How much is added each time?
engine.instruction-fix: Find the mistake and fix it.

continue-pattern.title: Continue the pattern
continue-pattern.prompt: Look at this pattern. The last three spaces are empty. Fill them with the shapes below.
continue-pattern.hint: Say it aloud: circle, triangle, triangle; circle, triangle, triangle; … What comes next?
continue-pattern.success: Well done! Red circle, blue triangle, blue triangle, and then it starts again.
continue-pattern.why: How did you know a circle comes after two triangles?
continue-pattern.model: Because these three repeat together: one red circle, then two blue triangles. After every two triangles, the circle comes back.

feedback.not-finished: There is still an empty space. Tap it and place a shape.
feedback.wrong-color: The shape is right but not the colour. Look at the colours too.
feedback.wrong-shape: The colour is right but not the shape. Circle or triangle?
feedback.wrong-item: One shape does not fit. Read the pattern from the start and go along.

find-the-unit.title: Find the unit of repeat
find-the-unit.prompt: One chunk of this pattern repeats. Tap the shape where the pattern starts again.
find-the-unit.hint: Two stars, two squares … what comes next? That is where the pattern starts again.
find-the-unit.success: Right! Star, star, square, square. That chunk repeats.
find-the-unit.why: Why is “star, star” on its own not the unit of repeat?
find-the-unit.model: Because after two stars another star does not come; a square does. The chunk that comes again and again has four shapes: star, star, square, square.

feedback.empty: Tap the shape where the pattern starts again.
feedback.unit-short: Too soon! That chunk does not come again straight after. Go a bit further.
feedback.unit-long: That is in the middle of the pattern. Find where star, star starts again.
feedback.unit-repeats: Your chunk is the unit twice over. Make it shorter.

fix-the-mistake.title: Fix the mistake
fix-the-mistake.prompt: One shape in this pattern is wrong. Tap it, then choose the right shape below.
fix-the-mistake.hint: The unit has three shapes: heart, circle, square. Check them one by one.
fix-the-mistake.success: Well done! Now the pattern is right: red heart, yellow circle, blue square.
fix-the-mistake.why: How did you find the wrong shape?
fix-the-mistake.model: After every red heart there should be a yellow circle. Space 5 had a blue circle. The shape was right but the colour was not.

feedback.wrong-color: One colour is still wrong. What colour are the circles?
feedback.wrong-shape: One shape still does not fit. What shape comes after a heart?
feedback.wrong-item: One space still does not fit. Read it from the start: heart, circle, square, …

matchsticks.title: Matchstick pattern
matchsticks.prompt: We made squares from matchsticks. Each figure has one more square. How many matchsticks are in figure 4 and figure 10?
matchsticks.hint: From figure 1 to figure 2, how many sticks were added? And from figure 2 to figure 3?
matchsticks.success: Right! 3 sticks are added each time: 4, 7, 10, 13, … Figure 10 has 31 sticks.
matchsticks.why: Why are 3 sticks added each time, not 4?
matchsticks.model: The new square is joined to the one before it. One of its sides is already there, so it needs only 3 sticks. Figure 10: the first stick plus 10 lots of 3 sticks, so 1 + 30 = 31.

feedback.empty: Write a number in both spaces of the table.
feedback.four-each: You counted 4 sticks for every square. But the squares share a side. Count figure 2 again.
feedback.forgot-first: Close! You forgot the very first stick on the left.
feedback.doubled: Figure 10 is not double figure 5: two separate figures would each have a first stick. Count on in 3s.
feedback.too-big: Too many. Only 3 sticks are added each time.
feedback.too-small: Too few. 3 sticks are added each time; count on from 10.

number-jumps.title: Number jumps
number-jumps.prompt: The numbers go up in equal jumps. Write the size of the jump and fill in the empty spaces.
number-jumps.hint: How many from 3 to 7? And from 7 to 11?
number-jumps.success: Well done! The numbers go up in 4s: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23.
number-jumps.why: If we carry on, will 40 be in this pattern? Why?
number-jumps.model: No. The pattern goes 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, 31, 35, 39, 43. It has 39 and then 43. 40 is in between.

feedback.empty: Fill in every empty space, and the size of the jump too.
feedback.wrong-step: The jump size is not right. Count from 3 to 7: 4, 5, 6, 7.
feedback.counted-start: You counted the 11 itself. Count on four from 11: 12, 13, 14, 15.
feedback.added-one: You only added one. The jumps are bigger.
feedback.too-big: One of the numbers is too big. Look at the jump size.
feedback.too-small: One of the numbers is too small. Look at the jump size.
